newsitem.title: USA: Sierra Health buying Physician Corp. for $434 million.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Health buying Physician Corp. for $434 million.

text.p: Sierra Health Services Inc. said Monday it agreed to buy Physician Corp. of America in a stock deal valued at $421 million in the latest move toward consolidation in the managed health care industry.
The combined company would be the eighth biggest in the United States and would provide services to 1.5 million customers from Nevada to Florida as well as Puerto Rico.

Las Vegas-based Sierra Health said it would offer 0.45 of its own shares for each of the 39.2 million outstanding shares of Physician Corp., a Miami-based managed care company with operations in Florida, Texas and Puerto Rico.
Sierra currently operates in Nevada and Houston, Texas.
"This merger represents an excellent strategic opportunity for Sierra to gain a strong multi-state presence," Sierra Chairman Dr. Anthony Martin said in a statement.
"We will be able to substantially broaden our existing service area in Texas, and become one of the market leaders in Florida and Puerto Rico."
But Sierra's stock fell sharply amid concerns the combination might not yield the same cost savings as other mergers of health maintenance organisations (HMOs) have done in the past.
Sierra stock fell $5 to $23.875 after the merger was announced, pushing the total value of the deal down to about $421 million from $509 million based on Friday's closing price.

Analysts said that in pursuing a merger that would make it a multi-state company, Sierra missed out on one of the biggest benefits of consolidation: getting greater leverage from an existing provider network.
At least two brokerage houses, Oppenheimer and Dillon Read, downgraded Sierra on expectations the merger would dilute earnings.

"The trick in consolidating is to have geographic overlap," said Dave Shove, an analyst with Fox-Pitt, Kelton. "But when a company in Las Vegas buys a company in Florida or Texas, there is no consolidation and it hasn't made the system any more efficient."
In adition to that problem, analysts noted that one of the states where Sierra chose to expand, Floria, is an especially tough market from a competitive and a regulatory standpoint.

The state's two big managed care companies, Humana Inc. and United Healthcare Corp., have a relatively strong market position, and regulators in Florida have allowed non-HMO health care plans to price their services below cost.
Sierra said the combined cmpany will have more than $2 billion in annual revenues. Erin MacDonald, currently president and chief operating officer of Sierra, will remain in those positions.

The combined company will be named Sierra Health Services Inc., with national headquarters in Las Vegas. The merger is expected to close by March 31, pending normal shareholder and regulatory approvals.
